about: Place-image style test (Josh, 2026-10-14): linocuts read as stereotyped or dated about half the time, and Josh's hypothesis is that a different art style per city makes exploring less samey and keeps people enjoying the art rather than critiquing a repeated style. Each city's places try that city's approved card style (docs/mexico-version.md), plus an abstract version, on two places, next to the current linocut. Run: COUNTRY=es-mx npm run style-test. Output: style-test/es-mx/index.html (not committed). Round 2 (Josh, 2026-10-14): city style wins, but CDMX, Guadalajara and San Miguel came out too similar (soft, flat, pastel). Each gets a distinct technique; Oaxaca and Puebla are settled and skipped. Oaxaca back in round 2 (Josh): folk art dialled up, defined by alebrije patterning, dotted outlines and the Zapotec greca border.
rules: Contemporary Mexico: today's clothes and objects, everyday life; no sombreros, cacti, skulls, rebozos or costumes. Lettering: only the place's own sign, word for word; no other words anywhere, no dates, no 'HOY', no neighbourhood or city names, no slogans, no brand names or logos. Keep the main scene in the centre; nothing important near the edges.

ciudad-de-mexico.style: Risograph print in two inks, hot pink and teal, with visible grain, slight misregistration between the two colours and flat overlapping shapes; contemporary and urban

oaxaca.style: Oaxacan folk-art painting in the manner of painted alebrije carvings: every surface covered in dense hand-painted patterns of dots, dashes, zigzags, scales and petals; outlines traced in rows of contrasting dots; flat, toy-like perspective; loud complementary colours side by side; a border of Zapotec step-fret (greca) pattern; one fantastical alebrije creature (a patterned winged jaguar, dragon-dog or lizard) appears in the scene as a carved figure on a shelf or painted on a wall; no skulls, no devils; a contemporary scene
oaxaca.colours: cochineal red, marigold, turquoise, magenta, lime green and indigo

puebla.style: Illustration in the style of a hand-painted Talavera tile panel from Puebla: slightly glossy glaze, visible brush marks, a thin decorative tile border. Palette: cobalt blue and white with touches of yellow, ochre and green
puebla.colours: cobalt blue and white with touches of yellow, ochre and green

guadalajara.style: Linocut print with bold carved black lines and wood-grain texture, strong contrast, in bright colour
guadalajara.colours: terracotta, teal, mustard and sky blue

san-miguel-de-allende.style: Mexican fresco mural: thick dark outlines, rounded monumental forms, rough plaster texture with visible cracks and patches, strong rhythmic composition; earth colours only
san-miguel-de-allende.colours: terracotta, ochre, rose, slate blue and deep green

abstract: Abstract colour-block composition: large flat overlapping shapes and a few confident lines suggest the place and the people in it, without detail; bold and contemporary; use the city's colours
